Hi Sofia —

Thanks for sending these over. No mutual NDA required for an initial redline from our side; we can proceed with the documents you shared. A few clarifying asks to make our first pass useful: 

1) Signer matrix: ChronoSys_Company_Info lists two authorized signers — can you confirm which role (legal or finance) will execute the MSA and which will sign order forms? That affects amendment/notice routing.

2) Section 10 (legacy retention): is the intent to preserve telemetry indefinitely under the internal policy or to move to a defined retention (e.g., 24 months)? If indefinite, we'll propose Redwood's standard capped telemetry retention and an export mechanism for requested logs.

3) Exhibit C tokenization: the spreadsheet has hourly totals but not tokenization assumptions. Can you share a representative sample payload or clarify the tokens-per-record expectation so we can model batching and burst handling?

We aim to return an initial redline with comments by COB Friday, Oct 24. Looping in Karthik (contracts) and Marissa (CS onboarding) so we can align on commercial and operational impacts.

Team — quick read-through highlights (high level):

• Section 7 (Indemnities): they’ve added an asymmetric IP carveout with a multiplier on damages. Recommend switching to our standard mutual IP indemnity and removing the multiplier — keeps commercial negotiations simple.

• Section 10 (Data Retention & Telemetry): if ChronoSys intends indefinite retention, propose our default of 24 months for telemetry with the option to export logs on request; note any regulatory exceptions.

• Section 14 (Export Controls): language is broad and could restrict certain overseas deployments; flag for review by Security/Compliance.

• Exhibit C (Capacity): the hourly buckets look fine but they’ve annotated short 10–15 minute spikes that exceed our standard burst policy. I’ll ask for a short sample payload and the expected tokenization assumptions so we can propose a batching strategy and pricing guardrails.

I’ll take the indemnity and retention redlines; Ben can draft the Exhibit C comments with Marissa for onboarding notes.

—Karthik

Hi Sofia / ChronoSys team —

Attached is our initial redline (tracked changes) and a short note on Exhibit C assumptions. Highlights:

• Retention (Sec 10): proposed defined telemetry retention of 24 months plus export on reasonable request.
• Indemnity (Sec 7): replaced the asymmetric IP multiplier with our mutual IP indemnity language; called out any third-party carveouts for later negotiation.
• Exhibit C: requested a sample payload and clarified tokens-per-record assumption; suggested a burst policy that covers short spikes up to 1.75x sustained for 15 minutes, and a recommended batching guide to reduce cost.

Next steps: please confirm signer roles (legal vs finance) and share a 3–5 record sample payload (sanitized) so Ben can finalize capacity sizing. If you want a short sync to walk through the redline, we have availability Mon/Tue next week.
